body:
> Prerequisite named by the /kanban:groom design (#191). Today `hkb archive` closes the card and leaves every card that was blocked by it pointing at a closed NOT_PLANNED issue — which `computeReady` never counts as done, so those children never promote. The groom plan's supersede rows are therefore handed back as by-hand recipes until this exists.

## What

- `hkb archive <n> --superseded-by <m>`: comment "Superseded by #m" on n, for every open child blocked by n add m as a blocker and remove n, then close n as not_planned; one line per edge moved; `--json` lists them. Without `--superseded-by`, `archive` refuses when n has open children and names them (today it silently strands them); `--force` keeps the old behaviour.
- Pure decision in `src/model.js` (children to move, children that would be stranded); I/O in lifecycle.js.

## Done when

- Fixture: n blocks two open cards → `archive n --superseded-by m` re-links both and closes n; plain `archive n` refuses naming them. `npm run lint && npm test` green.
goal: A superseded card is archived in one command that comments the pointer, moves its children under the survivor, and refuses when a child would be stranded
title: hkb archive --superseded-by <m>: close as a duplicate with a pointer, re-linking the children it would otherwise strand
